title: The clinic closes but the physician still has an EHR second shift at home
job: Clear results, refills, messages and admin tasks without missing the few items requiring urgent judgment.
trigger: Clinical day ends with unresolved inbox/tasks.
surfaceComplaint: I am still working in the EHR after I get home.
mechanism: High-risk and low-risk items share one attention surface. Poor routing and unclear ownership force physicians to inspect work that could be handled by staff, protocol or automation.

economics.painCostNote: AMA reports large weekly blocks on indirect care/admin and substantial after-hours EHR time for many physicians.

buyer.roiLogic: Recovering one physician hour/week can justify meaningful spend.

distribution.acquisition: Pilot at one clinic/team where protocols can change.

intervention.notBuildYet: No autonomous clinical advice or message sending.

experiment.sample: one clinic, 2 weeks of de-identified task metadata
experiment.artifactRequest: task type + routing history + timestamps + final owner
experiment.success: ≥30% fewer physician touches on safely delegable tasks with zero high-severity misses
experiment.kill: protocols too variable or EHR integration blocks routing changes

claims.text: AMA reports physicians averaged 13 hours/week on indirect patient care and 7.3 hours on administrative tasks in 2024 data.
22.5% reported more than eight hours/week of EHR work outside normal hours.
Exception-based routing is a safer first wedge than generating clinical responses.
